profile.reading:
This Lumen facility sits at 501 West 2nd Avenue in downtown Spokane, Washington, a coordinate that places it a few blocks south of the Spokane River and within the city's historic downtown core rather than in an industrial or suburban data center park. The operator is Lumen Technologies, the telecommunications company that traces its lineage through a series of mergers, CenturyLink's 2011 acquisition of Qwest Communications, itself a descendant of the old US West regional Bell operating company, and CenturyLink's 2017 merger with Level 3 Communications, before the combined company rebranded itself Lumen Technologies in 2020. That heritage matters for a building like this one, since a downtown address of this kind, close to a city core, is the pattern typical of a legacy incumbent local exchange carrier central office, a building originally built or adapted to house telephone switching equipment for the surrounding metro area, later repurposed for colocation and network interconnection as demand for that kind of space grew. No public building permit, county assessor record, or architectural history specific to 501 West 2nd Avenue was located in this pass to confirm whether this building was originally constructed as a telephone central office, so that reading is offered as a pattern match to Lumen's general facility type rather than a confirmed fact about this address.

Lumen does not publish site specific technical details for individual colocation locations on its public marketing pages. The company's own site describes its overall North American colocation footprint as more than 200 locations across more than 120 cities, serving more than 2,600 colocation customers, with cabinet and cage based space offered at power densities from roughly 3 kW to 12 kW, AC and DC power delivery options, N, 2N, and N+1 cooling and generator redundancy configurations depending on the site, and a network operations center monitoring the portfolio around the clock. Lumen states that more than 50 of its locations carry compliance certifications, without naming which ones, and advertises a 100 percent uptime service level commitment across its colocation portfolio. None of these figures are broken out by individual site, so no capacity, redundancy tier, or certification status specific to the Spokane location is recorded here, and none of Lumen's IT capacity, utility power, or generator figures for this address specifically were found in public sourcing.

Spokane itself is eastern Washington's largest city and a regional hub for the Inland Northwest, separate from the hydropower driven data center clusters of central Washington around Quincy and George, and separate from the Seattle metro market on the state's west side. A Lumen presence here fits the company's role as a national network operator maintaining points of presence and interconnection facilities across mid sized metro areas nationwide, rather than as a hyperscale or wholesale data center developer in the mold of operators building large purpose built campuses. No trade press coverage naming this specific Spokane facility, and no state or local government record referencing it by address, was found in this pass.
profile.research_note: WebSearch was exhausted this session (200 of 200) before this facility was reached, so research relied on direct WebFetch of Lumen's own about and colocation pages plus this database's own osm_tags, which supplied the confirmed 501 West 2nd Avenue, Spokane, WA 99201 address and the operator:wikidata match (Q5063092, Lumen Technologies) confirming operator identity. Lumen's marketing pages publish only aggregate national colocation network statistics (200+ locations, 120+ cities, 2,600+ customers, 3-12kW densities, N/2N/N+1 redundancy options, 50+ certified locations, 100% uptime SLA) with no per-site breakdown, so no Spokane-specific IT capacity, utility power, or generation figure exists to record. The central-office-heritage framing is offered as an informed pattern read based on the downtown address and Lumen/CenturyLink/Qwest/US West corporate history, not a confirmed building record, and is worded in the reading to make that distinction clear. No Spokane County Assessor or City of Spokane permit record was accessible in this pass.

reading.body:
Lumen operates this Spokane colocation facility as part of a network-centric edge product across 175-plus North American sites, not as a wholesale hyperscale campus. The operator publishes no per-building specifications, only a company-wide cabinet power range of 3 to 15 kilowatts varying by site, making it impossible to estimate the facility's total capacity, density, or relevance to large-scale AI compute deployment from disclosed facts.

Spokane County is emerging as a separate data center growth area from Eastern Washington's established Columbia Basin hydro cluster around Quincy and Wenatchee. Avista Utilities filed a nonbinding memorandum of understanding in May 2026 to supply an unnamed large customer with 125 megawatts starting in 2029, scaling to as much as 500 megawatts by 2032, equal to roughly 16 percent of Avista's current 3,000-megawatt system peak capacity. This deal still requires formal review by the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission before proceeding.

Among Washington's 46 mapped data center facilities, only two publish megawatt figures, totaling 60 megawatts disclosed capacity statewide. This Lumen facility ranks third by published capacity in the state, a ranking that reflects the absence of published specs from nearly all other mapped sites rather than a measure of its actual size or compute capability. Without disclosed power or space specifications, this facility cannot be assessed against the grid constraint that binds AI scaling.
